dataList.name: The Exemplar Fixer
dataList.desc: I saw two young Fixers huddled at the end of a stiflingly narrow street corner, poring over a magazine together. One of them wore a long coat that seemed made for someone at least twice his height. It was a comical sight, him fussing with the hems in a desperate bid to make them look remotely fitting. "How do I look? Getting there?" "Getting to look like a parody of that Fixer, maybe. Trust me, dude. There's only so much clothes can do to make the man, even if it's the same kind of coat he wears." "Tsk... Really? Still, it should at least help me feel badass... And what's being a Fixer if not all about that mindset...?" The other Fixer let out a sarcastic snort, then leaned toward us and whispered loudly. "Boy, am I glad to see some real Fixers out here. You are Fixers, right? At least you do look the part. Why don't you come talk some sense into him? Poor guy's been popping the collar in a hundred different ways for the last 30 minutes."

options.message: Give the young Fixer some genuine tips.
options.messageDesc: Sloth Advantage check. Pass to gain a Keywordless E.G.O Gift.

result:
"Uh... Cool coat, my guy."

"Could've, um, fooled me. It... fits you like a tailored suit."

The young Fixer beamed happily at the compliments.

"Sure does, doesn't it? Now check this out. I'm gonna rest this weapon on my shoulder all nonchalant like this... and bam! How do I look?"

... He looks like a small child desperately trying to look like a statuesque comic book character.

As we looked back and forth between his supposed attempt and the cover Fixer on the magazine, it slowly began to dawn on us that the difference between them was more than just sartorial; it was something on the metaphysical realm—it was a matter of "energy."

Being forced to sit through this one-man fashion show for a while slowly eroded away at the Sinners' patience until some of them finally decided to speak up.

"If I might ask, young sir—thou must be engaged in an attempt at the art of 'cosplay,' indeed? Hmm... Forsooth, I concede that certain physiological disparities cannot be replicated; alas, I insist that thou seekest a coat that may better complement thy stature..."

"Yeah, mate. Totally. Go 'round wearin' that shite for a week, and you'll get your own story in the magazines in no time. Don't ask me which section."

"... You're all so mean."

The Fixer huffed and strode away from us, dragging that long coat behind him all the way.

"*cough* I guess an honest conversation... could be an approach. Sorry about wasting your time."

dataList.name: Dawn Office
dataList.desc: Lured by a mysterious, pleasantly bitter scent, we stopped beneath a sign that read "Dawn Office." When we stepped inside, we saw an old man lounging on a couch, reading through papers, while a young man in glasses carefully set a steaming teacup in front of him. "Hmm... Are you here for a contract?" "Ah, I suppose you were drawn here by the smell. This tea has quite a pleasant aroma, doesn't it? We've brewed more than enough for everyone, so don't hesitate to take a cup or two." "Not enough for everyone here, Master..." The Fixer in glasses gave the pot a concerned glance. "Then please, have mine. Guests come first, after all."

options.messageDesc: Select to heal HP & SP for all allies
result:
Comforting warmth spread through the hands that cradled the teacups.
The Sinners' faces briefly scrunched up at the initial bitterness, but a gentle sweetness lingered after each sip.

By the time we emptied our cups, our shoulders—which had tensed up without us realizing—had finally relaxed.

"There's nothing wrong with keeping busy, but allow yourselves a brief respite with a nice cup of tea."
"Everyone needs a moment to unwind, hm?"

Following his own advice, the old man never once asked what had brought us there as we drank our tea.

dataList.name: The Knight of Despair
dataList.desc:
At the end of a dark passage, a lone knight stands beside a sword glowing blue.

As we approach, the knight silently regards our wounds before extending a hand.

"So... there is still something left to protect."

A bottomless sorrow hangs about the offered hand, while the tip of the sword floating nearby seems steeped in endless despair.

options.messageDesc: Pride Advantage check. Pass to gain a Keywordless E.G.O Gift.

options.message:
Offer the Sword Sharpened with Tears.
<size=75%><color=#a16a3b>Choice unlocked with the E.G.O Gift "Sword Sharpened with Tears"</color></size>
options.messageDesc: Select to gain a Sinking E.G.O Gift
result:
"This sword..."

The Knight gently lays a hand upon the blade we offer. A droplet of cold, black tear falls from her eye and seeps into its edge.

"A sword... forged and sharpened from vows that could never be kept..."
"All I have left is this hollow pride... but please, take it..."

We accept the sword from the Knight. An unfathomable despair creeps up the arm that holds it.

dataList.name: Wedge Office
dataList.desc: A sign reading "Wedge Office" hangs over an elegant, old-fashioned door. We knock cautiously, and two petite Fixers answered the door and received us. "You guys here to give us a contract?" "Is that any way to address a visitor? You should be more polite." "Oh, don't start. What do you want me to say?" "May I ask if you guys are here to commission a contract?" "... How's that supposed to be more 'polite'?" "It's called 'professional tone.' How ignorant can you be?" As the two Fixers, seemingly twins, bicker with each other, a man in a neat black coat emerges from the back room to greet us. "I don't believe we've met. You don't look like clients with a request... Are you looking for work?"

options.message: Ask if we can work with them.
options.messageDesc: Select to gain a Keywordless E.G.O Gift
result:
"You want to work with us?"

He studies us for a moment, then slowly shakes his head.

"You look capable in a fight, but I have no way of judging your battle analysis and decision-making skills just by looking at you."

"I doubt you could work in step with us just yet."

"Our sister Office might be a better fit, though."

He takes a white cravat from his desk drawer and hands it to us.

"Take this to Dawn Office. They value fighting ability more than we do."

He rises and sees us out with the other two Fixers.

"Perhaps we'll meet again someday."

options.message: Claim to be new recruits from their sister Office.
options.messageDesc: Select to gain a Tremor E.G.O Gift
result:
He looks us over one by one, then asks with a hint of suspicion.

"Which sister Office would that be?"

We hesitate, and his expression grows more doubtful. Then...

"'Tis D-Dawn Office!"

"Oh? Salvador didn't mention taking on any new hires."

"V-verily, that's—uh..."

Caught off guard, we stumbled through our answers, desperately piecing together whatever we knew to pass ourselves off as Dawn Office rookies.

"... I see. I believe I understand now."

He gets up, takes a black hat from the coat rack, and offers it to us.

"You certainly did your homework on Fixer Offices."

"But a word of advice: next time someone asks, don't go quite so far out of your way to explain yourself. It only makes you sound suspicious."

"I'm telling you, I was trying not to burst out laughing."

"Lies need practice too, you know."

We take the hat and step outside. As soon as the door closes, laughter erupts from within.

dataList.name: Wedge Office
dataList.desc:
At a counter tucked into an alley, two Fixers of markedly different heights are arguing with a clerk.

"It was a clean cut, you know. We retrieved the head after the whole situation was taken care of."

"My dear fellow, do you truly think we'd pay for such expensive stasis-preservation packaging just to commit insurance fraud?"

"According to the policy, you'll need to go back and recover the torso too before we can help—"

"Oh, c'mon. You can't be serious."

The shorter Fixer keeps her voice low, but her words cut sharply into the insurance clerk.

"I'm only an employee here. I have to follow the terms of your insurance policy."

"Then follow them. What's the problem? You're really getting on my nerves."

... It seems there's a dispute over an insurance claim.

How should we proceed?

options.messageDesc: Select to gain a Tremor E.G.O Gift
result:
"If there's no way to prove it, you have to go by the terms of the contract..."

"These kinds of things happen all the time in the City, you know."

"Are you calling us scammers? You're really pissing me off."

Just as the smaller Fixer starts to turn her spear toward us...

"With all due respect, Miss, persist with this conduct, and we'll have no choice but to remove you by force."

An employee who looks like a supervisor steps forward, holding a sharp-tipped cane.

"Let us return. ... We'll have to find a suitable prosthetic body instead."

"Damn insurance companies. Always the same crap."

"Next time, do read your policy carefully."

The two Fixers take their stasis-preservation case and leave.

"That was minutes away from becoming really nasty. Say, do you have insurance yourselves? We have a policy that's perfect for disputes like this. Why not hear me out? You'll even get a free gift just for the consultation! Now, the first thing about this plan is..."

It takes us more time than we were willing to spare to escape the clerk's sales pitch.

All we have to show for the time we've lost is a small promotional gift.

options.messageDesc: Select to gain a Pierce E.G.O Gift
result:
"Hm... There's a special clause here..."

"A special clause...? Where?"

We take a closer look at the insurance papers the Fixers are holding.

In tiny, almost transparent print, a rider states that the first claim is covered regardless of the cause.

"... I don't remember agreeing to that..."

"I did tell you to read things carefully before signing."

"... Whatever. This works out for us. Anyway, so it's covered, right?"

"... Dammit, that's the first-generation policy, isn't it? We revised it the day after release because the terms were so unfavorable... Fine, wait here. We'll process your claim as written."

The insurance clerk crumples the paperwork in frustration and retreats inside, grumbling.

"Thanks. Sharp eyes you've got."

"We don't really have anything else to give you right now... Here, take this."

"It's damaged, but the material is expensive. A good Workshop should pay a decent sum for it."

A little later, the two Fixers pick up their stasis-preservation case and head inside at the clerk's direction.
